facts: Pinned public SDK skill namespace exposes list only; no public skill.register/remove/reload in generated client. Do not invent a setter or overload config.update(shell).
ConfigSkillPlugin loads directory/document skill sources and registers a ctx.skill.transform hook. Refresh/reload follows file watcher and config.updated internally, not a public caller contract.

CompatibilityPlugin can scan Claude/agents skills, with different source precedence and file watchers. Existing project:false/filewatcher:false startup authority must not be weakened by generic project enablement.

Any next explicit runtime skill application needs a reviewed supported boundary, exact inert file observation and truthful source/active status. Saving a SKILL.md alone cannot establish activation under current runtime.
Current MCP increment remains active; these facts do not amend accepted MCP design or expand current implementation.

Separate from global skill.list namespace, public SDK session.skill exists: SessionSkillInput has sessionID/id/resume optional. This is existing-skill session activation, not global registration/remove/reload or inert file saving.

Actual core Session.skill resolves an existing Skill ID, publishes session.skill.activated containing id/name/text, then resumes execution unless input.resume===false. A future design must verify actual public RPC mapping and closed resume:false behavior before any runtime use; no provider/model consumption proof from source.
Current MCP rendered checks ongoing; this new source fact does not expand current run or select next feature. Existing no public global skill register/remove/reload finding remains valid.

Actual client EndpointSessionSkill sends params.sessionID and payload {id,resume}; actual server session.skill handler maps payload.id -> core skill and passes resume unchanged. Source confirms resume:false reaches core guard, still not executed runtime evidence. Public API has no caller-supplied messageID, so any future durable operation must verify original effect by bounded log/history baseline and hold uncertain correlation rather than replay.

Actual ConfigDiscovery.discover sets project directories empty when options.project===false. With global false, no project/compat global skill paths are discovered. Existing isolated startup cannot be described as loading edited workspace Skills.

Pinned Plugin Context has skill.transform/editor list/get/add/update/remove and skill.reload; rpc.register is available in plugin context. These are trusted in-process plugin APIs, not public global SDK mutation endpoints. A new trusted plugin/closed RPC boundary would be major and requires initial accepted design, scoped auth/lifetime/storage/compatibility proof before implementation.

Existing session.skill can activate only already registered Native Skill IDs; source-only existence is insufficient to promise an edited SKILL.md becomes available. Do not substitute AGENTS instructions.put for Skills semantics.

ServerProcess.start typed options expose config/project/content and no direct plugins option. Core Instance.layer(options.plugins) and SdkPlugins.register are separate embedding APIs; do not claim server-start supports injection without checking layer scope.

ConfigPlugin.Plugins accepts strings or {package,options}. PluginModule.load reports local/package source and an install option. A potential trusted built-in module route must prove exact bundled file loading, scope and no external install/user plugin discovery. These declarations alone are not runtime acceptance.

Actual pinned SkillFile.parse uses Markdown frontmatter optional name/description/metadata, ID from parent folder for SKILL.md, display name defaults to that ID, Native content is markdown body, and metadata[opencode/autoinvoke] accepts boolean or true/false strings. Do not assume arbitrary other vendor fields or that full on-disk frontmatter equals Native content.

Current configuration-save-kernel is descriptor-only Darwin arm64/Bun1.4.2, closed kind instructions|mcp, fixed root leaf AGENTS.md|opencode.json. Skills nested publication is not currently supported; next design must explicitly preserve ancestor/root/file identity and existing publication/backup semantics rather than pass renderer arbitrary path.
